questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 9 % 2 + I is 1 + I, so the test is I <= I + 1, which is always true. X = (3I + 2I) / I = 5 for every I, so 5 is printed forever.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The semicolon after for (I = 1; I < 10; ) is an empty loop body. I is never incremented in the for-header, so I < 10 stays true and the loop never ends. The block that updates J and I is not part of the for-loop. This is a hang, not a runtime exception. (If the semicolon were removed, J would become 25, and the printed message would still be wrong because 1+3+5+7+9 are odd numbers.)

questions.question: Which statement is correct among the mentioned statements? i. The for loop works faster than a while loop ii. for( ; ; )implements an infinite loop

options.text: Both i and ii are correct
Both i and ii are incorrect

questions.explanation: for (;;) has an omitted condition, which is treated as true, so it is an infinite loop. A for loop is not inherently faster than an equivalent while loop; that depends on the body and the JIT, not the keyword.

questions.question: Which of the C# code should be added to get the following output?
questions.explanation: A decreasing triangle needs an inner loop from j = i to 4 (5, 4, 3, 2, then 1 stars). Console.Write prints on the same line; Console.WriteLine() ends the row. Option a prints a 5x5 rectangle, option d prints an increasing triangle, and option b's inner loop (j = 4; j <= i; j--) does not run for i < 4. (The original options used console.WriteLine, which would not compile: Console is case-sensitive, and WriteLine would put each star on a new line.)

questions.question: Which of the following is not an infinite loop in C#?
questions.explanation: A for-loop condition must be a bool. for (; false; ) never enters the body, so it is not infinite. for (;;) and for (; true; ) and while (true) all loop forever. (The original options used C-style integer conditions such as for (;0;), which do not compile in C# because int cannot be converted to bool.)

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Start: i = 1, j = 1, so i == j and continue skips printing. Next: i = 2, j = 0; the condition holds and 0 is printed. Next: i = 3, j = -1, but j >= 0 is false so the loop ends.

Output:

0
